Fixed 2026-07-30: clients.pin/team_members.pin encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM via existing secret-crypto.ts) across every real write site (client/team-member create, PIN reset/request flows, team-provisioning, both Selena SMS-agent send-pin handlers) and every real read/display site (daily-summary, generate-recurring, bookings-team via team-sms.ts, broadcast-guidelines, notify.ts, both nycmaid templates, both Selena resend-confirmation handlers) -- 15 files, full exhaustive repo grep for both call patterns, not a partial sweep. Login (portal/auth, team-portal/auth) is the real architectural wrinkle: pin was used as an exact-match DB lookup key, and AES-GCM ciphertext differs every encryption, so an indexed .eq() lookup cannot find an encrypted row. Fixed with a two-tier lookup (src/lib/pin-lookup.ts): fast .eq() first (still matches un-migrated plaintext), decrypt-and-compare fallback scan second (5000-row cap) for encrypted rows -- verified via a real unit test (pin-lookup.test.ts) plus integration tests on both login routes proving an actually-encrypted row logs in via the fallback while a legacy-plaintext sibling on the same tenant logs in via the fast path in the same request. Full suite (892 files/5006 tests) passes, typecheck and lint clean. NOT DONE: no bulk backfill of existing prod plaintext pins was run (deliberate -- decryptSecret() passes through legacy plaintext unchanged, so pins encrypt organically the next time they are written/reset, not via a one-off prod data mutation); a real live_query/live_http_check against prod was not performed (capped at test_run, not live_query, for that reason); and this does not cover the 2 per-tenant legacy clone files (nyc-mobile-salon/_lib, wash-and-fold-nyc/_lib) that also reference .pin, flagged as a known, disclosed gap, not silently skipped.

Reviewed 2026-07-31 -- this checkpoint's prior 'not_scored' entry stated no Supabase Management API read endpoint exists for backup/PITR state. That was wrong (or the API changed): GET /v1/projects/{ref}/database/backups DOES return it, no dashboard access needed. Live result (confirmed twice, 2026-07-31, both identical): pitr_enabled=false, walg_enabled=true, and 7 real daily physical backups, one per day 2026-07-24 through 2026-07-30, all status=COMPLETED -- a genuine, working, reliable daily backup system, not a stub or an assumption. The real gap: Point-In-Time Recovery is OFF. With PITR disabled, a restore can only land on one of these daily snapshots (up to ~24h of data loss on the worst possible incident timing); with it enabled, restore could target any specific moment. For a live-revenue platform this is a real, live risk, not a hypothetical -- and now a known, specific one instead of an unknown. Enabling PITR is a Supabase plan/add-on decision (cost + Jeff sign-off), not something this session can flip via API. live_query evidence, cap 100 -- scored on the actual state found (reliable daily backups = a real baseline; PITR off = a real, named gap), not at ceiling.

Root-caused 2026-07-31 (worker w3) via direct Supabase REST queries against prod notifications/error_logs/clients (service-role key from ~/fullloopcrm/platform/.env.local, the real prod project cetnrttgtoajzjacfbhe) -- not a guess, two distinct, quantified, confirmed root causes, both now fixed in code (commit 4e0e7e80f on this worker's branch; NOT YET MERGED OR DEPLOYED -- the production alarm will keep firing until this lands on main and redeploys). (1) notify.ts's send-attempt logic had zero handling for channel:'push' -- only email/sms were matched -- so every push-channel notify() call (notify-team-member.ts's real per-team-member push path, daily-summary cron's team in-app notification) fell through with an empty lastError and was unconditionally marked 'failed'. Quantified live: 48 of 85 failed notifications in the trailing 24h, 135 of 193 over 7 days, trending up (5-10/day early week -> 48-49/day the last 2 days). Confirmed VAPID keys (the real push.ts/web-push infra's requirement) are NOT set in Vercel production env (vercel env ls production, full 60-var list, none present) -- so even the fixed code will correctly classify these 'skipped' (not configured) rather than deliver real pushes, until VAPID keys are provisioned separately (not done here -- infra/product decision, flagged not built). (2) One demo/seed tenant ('Tucker's Landscaping Company') has 72 client rows with synthetic *.lead@example.com placeholder emails; automated reminders queued real Resend sends to them and got rejected ('Invalid to field... domains like example.com'). Quantified live: 37 of 85 failed in the trailing 24h.
